claims: The Artemis II mission successfully launched on April 1, 2026.
The Artemis II mission launched at 6:35 p.m. EDT (2235 UTC).
The Artemis II mission launched from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B.
The Artemis II mission is crewed.
The Artemis II mission lifted off atop the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
The Artemis II mission is a 10-day journey around the Moon.
The launch window for the Artemis II mission opened at 6:24 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II mission launched from NASA's Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
The Artemis II mission is the first crewed flight to the Moon since 1972.
The crew of the Artemis II mission is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II mission length is 10 days.
The launch vehicle for the Artemis II mission is the Space Launch System (SLS).
The spacecraft for the Artemis II mission is the Orion Capsule.
If a launch delay had occurred on April 1 for the Artemis II mission, NASA had a two-hour window available.
Backup launch opportunities for the Artemis II mission were available later in the week.
